methodological_questions: How is portability operationalized for movers, and against what decoy or baseline?
Is n=24 enough to compare two profile groups?
How reliable are play-type-derived role labels across seasons and teams?
How can menu-similarity, teammate and system confounding and regression to the mean be controlled for movers?

historical_evidence.finding: Portability analysis of movers (428 pass n_decoys>=3; n=92 in KW-calibrated draft). KW p=0.047 across role classes was population-level; organizer-vs-connector gap (MW p=0.07, bootstrap CI [-0.001,+0.180]) had a CI including 0 after correcting a menu-similarity confound (gap CI [-1.47,+11.65]). Verdict recorded as inconclusive; limited by confounding and small sample.
Play-type profile similarity of replacement teammates did not separate absorption from cascade (similarity +0.863 vs +0.848; Spearman -0.19, wrong-signed); limited by label/classification error.
Flat DRIVE lifts across lags collapsed under within-team baseline; team-quality confound. Raw pooled effects with large n gave p~0 but d~0.01-0.03.
Global play-type lag lifts disappeared after team-season demeaning.
DRIVE PPP is 0.286 lower in playoffs than regular season across 25 teams (1.198 vs 0.912), with no CIs. DRIVE value is context-dependent.
DRIVE PPP did not decline across playoff series; no clear signal; selection caveats.
DRIVE efficiency rose rather than fell within games (+0.078 to +0.093).
Player-channel cells with n of 15-54 gave large lifts and team-level lifts small; flagged as exposure-sparse.
Position and low-volume check on structural load was abandoned with no results recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Role-class comparison of portability among movers (organizer vs connector)
failed_approaches.why: Menu-similarity confound; once corrected, the gap CI included 0 (artifact; confounding and small sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type profile similarity to explain absorb vs cascade
failed_approaches.why: Wrong-signed, no separation; label or classification error.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooled play-type effect estimates without team baseline
failed_approaches.why: Team-quality confounding produced apparent effects that vanished within team.
Insufficient exposure (n=15-54 per cell); no holdout.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on role portability among movers found that apparent differences between role classes were confounded by menu similarity and did not survive correction (FAM:SF-CHT-087, artifact/inconclusive).
Pooled play-type effects in this project have repeatedly collapsed under within-team controls (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-073).
DRIVE-based value varies by context (regular season vs playoff) (FAM:SF-APPS-011), which matters for drive-heavy portability comparisons.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shapers specifically differ from drive-heavy shapers in portability; no retrieved record tests that contrast.
Whether 'shaper' is a defined role label in the project; the retrieved records do not define it (the glossary was not consulted).
How the 24 units were defined, and whether they are players, movers, or player-moves.
Whether portability has a validated measure with adequate reliability.
own_inferences: With n=24 split between two profile groups (perhaps 8-16 per group, possibly fewer if cut-heavy shapers are rare), only large effects would be detectable. Prior comparable contrasts at n=92 were already borderline, so a test at n=24 is probably underpowered.

Cut-heavy players often play off-ball around stars or rim runners, so their play-type profile may track teammate and system context; a cut-vs-drive portability difference could simply reflect menu similarity or role-class differences already shown to confound.
The statement is directional and vague ('travel better', undefined). Without a pre-specified metric, many forks are available, which inflates false positives.
Role labels that depend on post-move play-type shares are partly outcome-derived: a player whose profile persists will 'travel' by construction.
uncertainties: Definition of 'shaper' and the cut-heavy/drive-heavy thresholds.
Definition of portability (profile persistence, influence retention, or efficiency).
Whether the 24 units are independent and what share are movers.
The records were not read in full beyond CHT-087; the other records were seen only as retrieval excerpts.
Possible overlap between the new question and Paper 1 portability work that was not retrieved.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history this might look like a simple two-group comparison to run as proceed. The retrieved record FAM:SF-CHT-087 showed that a closely related role-class portability gap became non-significant once menu similarity was controlled, and that team-level confounds repeatedly produced artifacts. That moved the decision to proceed_with_changes: a confound-controlled, pre-specified, mostly estimation-focused analysis, with a likely-inconclusive result expected.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 split across two role groups gives power only for very large differences; the closest earlier analysis (n=92) was inconclusive.
Menu similarity, team system and teammate quality affect portability and were shown to remove an earlier role-class gap.
'Role travels' and 'shaper' are undefined; role labels from play-type shares may be unstable across teams and seasons.

prior_work.summary: Related portability work compared organizer vs connector role classes among movers and found a gap that did not survive a menu-similarity correction. No retrieved record compares cut-heavy with drive-heavy shapers directly. The retrieved work cautions that pooled play-type effects are prone to confounding artifacts.

risks.text: n=24 units; per-group n is smaller and the contrast is a between-group difference with wide CIs.
Menu similarity between old and new team, usage, teammate quality, coach and system, and age. These produced artifacts in FAM:SF-CHT-087 and FAM:SF-CHT-029.
If cut-heavy/drive-heavy classification or shaper status uses post-move data, or portability is defined by profile persistence, the result is partly mechanical.
Cut counts are sparse and noisy per player-season, so cut-heavy classification may be unstable and regress.
Players selected for extreme cut or drive share will regress toward the mean after moving, which looks like poor portability for the more extreme group.
Few possessions per player in the new team, especially for a cut-heavy off-ball role and in playoffs.
Many possible portability metrics, thresholds, and season-pair choices could be tried.
Play-type value differs between regular season and playoffs (FAM:SF-APPS-011) and play-by-play-derived labels may shift across 2022-26.
Derived play-type records come from play-by-play parsing, so initiator and play-type labels have error, which affects cut vs drive classification.

design.estimand: Difference between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers in the change in a pre-specified portability index (pre-move vs post-move retention of the role's structural influence and play-type profile), net of destination-team menu similarity, reported as an effect size with a confidence interval, not as a significance test only.
design.unit: Player-move (a shaper who changes team between consecutive seasons within 2022-23 to 2025-26). The 24 units are assumed to be these; confirm their definition and independence (players with several moves are clustered).
design.sample: All shapers meeting a pre-registered definition (to be fixed from the project glossary before data inspection) with a minimum possession threshold in both teams, classified as cut-heavy or drive-heavy by pre-move shares only (for example top vs bottom tercile of cut share minus drive share, thresholds fixed in advance). Regular season only for the primary analysis; playoffs excluded or reported separately.
design.power: At n=24 (about 12 per group), 80% power at alpha=0.05 requires roughly d>=1.2. State this in advance. If the group split is unbalanced or per-group n<8, report only descriptive estimates with bootstrap CIs and declare the test underpowered. Tolerance for conclusions: a CI that excludes 0 and a minimum meaningful difference set in advance. Preferably extend the unit pool, e.g. to all movers as in the 428-mover pool, with profile share treated as a continuous predictor.
design.controls: Pre-move profile measured on pre-move data only; portability outcome measured on post-move data with a menu-similarity covariate (similarity of the old and new teams' play-type menus), usage, minutes, age, team-season demeaning, and use of decoy or matched-baseline comparison as in prior portability work. Use a reliability check (split-half of cut and drive shares) and a regression-to-the-mean correction (shrink shares or use a comparison group of non-movers with the same pre-profile).
design.falsification: Placebo: apply the same contrast to non-movers across consecutive seasons (no change of team) and to shuffled group labels; expect no group difference. Negative control: a metric unrelated to role (e.g. free-throw rate) should show no group difference. If cut-heavy shapers show an advantage only before menu-similarity adjustment, classify the result as an artifact, as in FAM:SF-CHT-087.
design.multiplicity: One primary portability index and one primary contrast, declared before analysis. Any alternative indices, thresholds, or playoff analyses are secondary and labelled exploratory, with Holm correction across them.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the adjusted difference favors cut-heavy shapers, the 95% bootstrap CI (clustered by player) excludes 0, the effect exceeds the pre-set minimum, and the placebo and negative-control checks are null. Rejected if the CI lies within the pre-set equivalence margin (only possible if the pool is extended). Otherwise report as inconclusive/underpowered; do not treat the result as a role-type claim.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type graph database for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, using the snapshot dated 2026-08-08 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13). Freeze the snapshot and the classification code hash before analysis.

methodological_questions: How is role portability or transferability operationalized when players change teams?
Is n=24 units sufficient to compare cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers?
How reliable are play-type-derived role labels across seasons and teams?
How to control for teammate and system confounding and regression to the mean when players move?
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers maintain their role and influence after changing teams better than drive-heavy shapers? Role stability and portability of structural roles in NBA play-by-play derived play-type data, 2022-23 to 2025-26.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
